sources_fast.name: capacitor bank
sources_fast.reason: capacitors discharge on any time scale; 99.5 MJ in 25 us is 6.25 TW peak (largest magnet-driver bank 50 MJ; TW-class power stays state of the art down to a 156 us rise at this energy)

sources_fast.name: motor-generator (flywheel and rectifier)
sources_fast.reason: a rectified alternator cannot rise in less than about a half-cycle of its output (10 ms); the request is 400x faster

sources_fast.name: homopolar generator
sources_fast.reason: at <= 600 V a rotor storing 99.5 MJ is a 553 F capacitor: even into its own ~500 nH it needs 26.1 ms to peak, 1.04e+03x slower than asked; an inductive store with an opening switch shortens the pulse but passes at most 25% of the energy to a load inductor

sources_fast.name: explosive flux-compression generator
sources_fast.reason: delivers tens of MA in microseconds (99.5 MJ against ~30 MJ demonstrated: extrapolation) but is consumed by every shot, usually with its load: an experiment, not a production source

sources_slow.name: capacitor bank
sources_slow.reason: capacitors discharge on any time scale; 99.5 MJ in 10 ms is 15.6 GW peak (largest magnet-driver bank 50 MJ; TW-class power stays state of the art down to a 156 us rise at this energy)

sources_slow.name: motor-generator (flywheel and rectifier)
sources_slow.reason: needs 15.6 GW and 99.5 MJ per pulse against the 1.4 GW, ~600 MJ-per-pulse motor-generator at Los Alamos: aspirational; right for a slow outer platform coil, not for an eddy-current pulse

sources_slow.name: homopolar generator
sources_slow.reason: at <= 600 V a rotor storing 99.5 MJ is a 553 F capacitor: even into its own ~500 nH it needs 26.1 ms to peak, 2.61x slower than asked; an inductive store with an opening switch shortens the pulse but passes at most 25% of the energy to a load inductor

sources_slow.name: explosive flux-compression generator
sources_slow.reason: an explosive generator is swept by its detonation in <~ 1 ms; it cannot stretch its pulse to 10 ms
